You write tests/compiler/directive.examples.test.ts only, a new file in place of the old one (every test of the old file pinned the old text). Import outputDirective from "../../src/compiler/directive.js". One test(...) per Output Directive example 1-4, in order, named "Output Directive example <n>: <what>"; example 2 compares with toBe against the one-target text of docs/TASK_P9b_runloop.md section 2.2 for src/a.ts, written out in full; then at most 8 of your own on section 2.2 (the several-targets text in full for ["src/a.ts", "tests/a.test.ts"], no trailing newline). The tests write nothing and spawn nothing. Import only what you use; eslint rejects an unused import; import test and expect from "vitest".

The examples below are the criterion, and you are its independent author: write one test per example (no fewer, no merging), and each test's docstring names the Function and the example number, e.g. `Output Directive example 1`.

Examples of Function Output Directive:
1. given targets [src/a.ts, tests/a.test.ts]; when the directive is rendered; then it begins 'This card writes 2 files. Return each one as a line `FILE: <path>`', holds the line block 'in this order:
src/a.ts
tests/a.test.ts

' (the two paths in that order), and ends 'so no line of a file may begin with three backticks.'
2. given targets [src/a.ts]; when the directive is rendered; then exactly 'Return the complete content of src/a.ts as ONE fenced block, and nothing else:

```
<the complete content of src/a.ts>
```

The opening fence may name the file's language. Only the FIRST fenced block of the answer becomes the file: a second block (a diff, an edit summary, an example) is dropped, and every line outside the fence is discarded. An answer with no fence at all is written to the file verbatim, prose and all. An answer whose fences do not pair up is discarded unread as cut off, so no line of the file may begin with three backticks. No preamble, no closing commentary, no diff, no elision: the whole file.'
3. given targets [docs/B.md, src/b.ts, tests/b.test.ts]; when the directive is rendered; then it begins 'This card writes 3 files.'; every fence line in it is exactly '```' (no language tag); it holds 'docs/B.md
src/b.ts
tests/b.test.ts
' in that order
4. given targets []; when the directive is rendered; then throws an Error whose message starts 'outputDirective'
